text:
The user switched Sora's walk to a simpler "idle shuffle" and wants your suggestions to refine it. Attached: (1) the forward shuffle sheet (4x2, 7 drawings, 8th cell blank), (2) a GIF of idle -> four shuffle steps -> idle, (3) the battle idle frame it starts from.




How it works now:

- The upper body is exactly the approved battle idle (wide guard crouch, both hands on the Kingdom Key handle low between the thighs, blade out to the right, three-quarter view facing right). Only the legs move.

- The front foot slides 0.30 m forward with a 1.2-1.8 cm lift (drawings 2-4), then the back foot slides up behind it (drawings 5-7). Drawing 1 is the idle stance itself, so there are no start or brake transitions: he walks straight out of the idle, and on release he finishes the current step and stands.

- The body sits midway between the feet, so planted feet never slide in Godot. The hips dip up to 7.5 cm while the feet are spread so the legs can reach from the already-wide idle stance (the grip sinks with the hips).

- Timing at 60 fps: holds [3,3,3,4,3,3,3] = 22 game frames per step; 54 px per step, about 148 px/s. The backward shuffle is the same loop reversed.

- The user just asked for it to be faster and cover more distance, which this version does (it was 28 frames and 40 px per step).




Constraints to keep: the idle's upper-body pose, the two-handed grip and the three-quarter screen angle must stay the same, and drawing 1 must stay identical to the idle so no transitions are needed.




What would you suggest Claude change to refine this shuffle so it looks better while staying this simple? Please give concrete values on the rig (bones: center, hara, mune, kubi, atama, L/R_kata, ude1, ude2, te, buki, momo, sune, ashi1, ashi2).
